newsitem.title: UK: UK'S Labour will set low inflation target - Brown.
newsitem.headline: UK'S Labour will set low inflation target - Brown.

text.p: HARROGATE, England (Nov 11) - A British Labour government will have a target for low and stable inflation and meet it, opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Monday.
"Labour in government will have a target for low and stable inflation," Brown told the Confederation of British Industry's annual conference.

"And...we will not be satisfied with talking as tough as the Tories. For unlike the government, we plan to deliver on our inflation target. We will want our inflation performance to match that of our competitors in Europe."
The Conservative government has 2.5 percent target for annual underlying inflation. Underlying inflation, excluding mortgage interest payments was 2.9 percent year-on-year in September.

Brown said interest rates should never again be used for short-term party political ends. To that end, a Labour government would establish a monetary policy committee for the Bank of England to bring more openness to the monetary policy process.
He also reiterated Labour's plans for fiscal prudence.
"Over the economic cycle, government will only borrow to finance public investment and not to fund public consumption," he said.
"We will keep the ratio of government debt to GDP stable on average over the economic cycle and at a prudent and sensible level."
There could not be any return to the high marginal tax rates imposed in the 1960s and 1970s, Brown said.
